title: build-findings-batch.v1 — one review round's findings, in one file
description: The batch input both recording verbs read (StarshipSuperjam/engine-template#1060). Recording a round used to be one invocation per finding, each carrying about a dozen flags; a session assembling thirty of those in shell loops is where a real failure happened — repeated --finding values built from a shell array collapsed into a single string, so the receipt demanded one bogus id and the step had to be redone. This is not a token saving: the summaries and rationales are the payload either way. It removes a class of quoting and ordering mistakes. ONE FILE, BOTH VERBS: `review record --findings-from-file` takes the ids for its receipt and `finding record --from-file` takes the dispositions, so a receipt's ids and the findings recorded against it are the same list by construction and cannot drift. ALL OR NOTHING: every entry is validated — this schema, then the cross-field refusals the per-flag form applies — before anything is written, and the write is one mutation, so a malformed entry records nothing.

schema_version.description: Names what this document is. A batch that does not say is refused rather than guessed.

stage.description: The review this batch belongs to. A batch names its own stage so a file cut for one review cannot be replayed against another; the verb refuses a mismatch instead of recording under the wrong key.

findings.description: The round's findings. May be empty — a lens that found nothing still records a receipt, and naming the same empty batch at both verbs keeps that honest.

finding.description: One finding and the session's disposition of it. The reviewer owns the severity; the session owns the disposition and whether it blocks — reviewer severity never chooses the remedy.

id.description: This round's id for the finding, as named in the receipt that demands it.

lens.description: The reviewer that raised it. `review record` refuses a batch carrying a lens other than the one whose receipt it is recording, because a receipt answers for what ITS lens found.

escalation_kind.description: The operator-owned decision boundary. Required on an escalated finding and refused on any other.

blocks_this_pr.description: Whether this finding still holds the pull request. Must agree with the disposition: a settled disposition (accepted-fixed, accepted-tracked, rejected) cannot also block, and an escalated one always does. The contradiction is refused at record time rather than interpreted at gate time.

operator_summary.description: The operator-safe text the merge-surface disagreement line is built from. Required on a blocking-severity finding that no longer blocks: the gate got quieter, the disclosure did not.

private_reference.description: Local-only reviewer note. Kept in build-state, never published to the pull-request body (StarshipSuperjam/engine-template#981).
